key_insight: LLM agents can run the correct simulation yet answer incorrectly when retrieved tool reports are replaced by non-authoritative evidence.
engineering_relevance: Scientific agent harnesses should identify authoritative outputs and evaluate evidence use separately from simulation correctness.
method: Evaluated agents on 158 execution-verified multiple-choice questions using the deterministic PHREEQC geochemistry simulator.
Compared in-context reports with section-index retrieval and replayed 11,007 logged simulator calls.
Tested fixed-simulation comparisons, authoritative-output guidance, inlining, and rounding instructions.
evidence_signal: Section-index retrieval reduced GPT-5.1 and GPT-5.2 accuracy by 11.3 and 7.9 percentage points, respectively, while neither Claude model showed a detectable cost.
watch_item: Effects vary by model, and unchanged final accuracy can conceal evidence-use losses offset by more frequent correct simulations.
paper_title: Same Simulation, Different Evidence: Where Retrieved Tool Output Costs LLM Agents Accuracy
